look:0.line: 'Give yourself a different *look* before you pass that counter.'

benefit:0.en: The back office of the market smelled of burnt wiring. A clerk offered me a seat and a warm cup. I did not sit. 'There is no *benefit* to staying silent,' I told him, sliding the drive onto his desk. He stared at it for a long moment, then reached for his radio.
benefit:0.cnHint: 我告诉那名职员，沉默对他没有任何____。
benefit:0.hook: His finger hovered over the call button.
benefit:0.line: 'There is no *benefit* to staying silent now.'

contain:0.en: Ali found the locked drawer and forced it open with a blade. Inside was a single envelope. 'This must *contain* the access codes,' she said, holding it to the light. The envelope was sealed with red wax pressed into the shape of a crow. Neither of us touched it yet.

contain:0.hook: The wax crow seemed to watch us.
contain:0.line: 'This must *contain* the codes — do not open it alone.'

direction:0.en: The server room split into four dark corridors. Grey Crow was gone. My earpiece gave one burst of static, then his voice: 'Follow the cable on the left wall. It will give you *direction*.' I pressed my hand to the cold wall and found the cable. It hummed under my fingers.

direction:0.line: 'Follow that cable — it will give you *direction*.'

attach:0.en: Ali showed me the tiny transmitter, no bigger than a coin. 'You have to *attach* it to the underside of his tray before he sits down,' she said. The food hall was packed. The target was three tables away, moving fast, tray already in hand. I had maybe ten seconds.

attach:0.hook: He turned, and our eyes met.
attach:0.line: '*Attach* it to the tray before he sits — go now.'

human:0.en: The night market hummed beneath the dome of Harbor City's old port district. I pushed through crowds of vendors and buyers, searching for Grey Crow. human:0.cnHint: 在嘈杂的夜市中，叙述者从耳机里捕捉到一个真实的____声音，意识到有人正在现场广播。

human:0.line: 'That *human* voice in the noise — it did not come from any machine.'

large:0.en: Grey Crow led me to a *large* storage room behind a spice stall — walls lined with crates, a single lamp swinging overhead. Ali was already inside, bent over a cracked screen. 'Zero left this here,' she said. The files on the screen held more names than I expected.
large:0.cnHint: 在一个____的储藏室里，阿栗发现了零点遗留的屏幕，上面的文件令人震惊。

large:0.line: 'A *large* list of names — and yours is near the top.'

derive:0.en: The night market hummed below, but I was inside the old signal tower. Grey Crow spread a coded map across the table. 'You can *derive* the safe route from these light patterns,' he said. Each neon flash outside was a clue. I traced the path with one cold finger.
derive:0.cnHint: 格雷·克罗展示地图，我试图从霓虹灯的闪烁规律中____出安全路线。
derive:0.hook: Then one light went dark — the wrong one.
derive:0.line: 'You can *derive* the answer from what the lights are telling you.'

report:0.en: Ali slid a folded paper across the noodle shop counter. 'This *report* came from the underground press,' she whispered. report:0.cnHint: 阿里在面馆里递来一份地下出版物的____，上面圈出了我的名字。
report:0.hook: Someone had circled my name before I even took the case.
report:0.line: 'This *report* has your name on it — read the last line.'

research:0.en: The back room of the tea house smelled of old paper. Grey Crow had covered every wall with notes. 'Months of *research*,' he said quietly, 'and it all points to one building.' I studied the web of threads and photographs. Somewhere in that tangle was the truth I had been chasing.
research:0.cnHint: 格雷·克罗在茶馆密室里展示数月____的成果，所有线索都指向同一栋建筑。
research:0.hook: The building on the map had been torn down ten years ago.
research:0.line: 'All my *research* leads to one place — and you will not like it.'

different:0.en: Zero sat across from me in the dim arcade, his voice flat. 'You think this city is *different* from the old ones,' he said, 'but every city hides the same rot.' He placed a small chip on the table between us. The arcade machines blinked and died, one by one.
different:0.cnHint: 在昏暗的游乐厅里，零点告诉我这座城市和其他城市并没有什么____。
different:0.hook: When the last screen went black, Zero was already gone.
different:0.line: 'You think Harbor City is *different*, but every city bleeds the same.'

author:0.en: The banned book had no cover, no title. Ali pointed to a tiny mark on the last page. 'The *author* always signs this way,' she said, 'a single crow feather, drawn in grey ink.' My chest tightened. I knew only one person who used that symbol, and he was supposed to be dead.
author:0.cnHint: 阿里在禁书最后一页发现了____独特的署名标记，那是一根灰色羽毛。
author:0.hook: I knew that symbol — and its owner was supposed to be dead.
author:0.line: 'The *author* of this book is someone you have already met.'

increase:0.en: Grey Crow pulled up the data on a cracked screen in the back of the print shop. The number of blocked signals showed a sharp *increase* over the past three nights. increase:0.cnHint: 在印刷店后室，格雷·克罗的屏幕显示过去三晚信号屏蔽次数急剧____。
increase:0.hook: The next spike on that graph would mean someone had been caught.
increase:0.line: 'This *increase* in blocked signals means the hunt has already started.'

university:0.en: The old *university* library had been sealed since the language riots of 2071. Ali had a key. Inside, rows of dusty terminals still glowed faintly, powered by a line no one had ever cut. 'The answers are in here,' she said. Her voice echoed off walls lined with forgotten words.
university:0.cnHint: 阿里带我进入封闭多年的旧____图书馆，那里的终端机至今仍在运转。
university:0.hook: One terminal showed a file opened just six hours ago.
university:0.line: 'This *university* was shut down because of what its students discovered.'

turn:0.en: I followed the corridor behind the night-market stalls, counting doors. Grey Crow had said to take the third *turn* on the left, then stop. I did. The wall in front of me was covered in coded graffiti, fresh paint still wet. Someone had left this message tonight, knowing I would come.
turn:0.cnHint: 我按照格雷·克罗的指示在夜市后巷____向，发现了一面刚刚写好的密语涂鸦。
turn:0.hook: The paint was still wet — they knew exactly when I would arrive.
turn:0.line: 'Take the third *turn* and you will see what they left for you.'

end:0.en: The night market tunnel stretched beneath Harbor City's oldest block. I walked its full length, past noodle stalls and humming signal boosters, until I reached the *end* — a rusted door, sealed with a code lock. Grey Crow had promised answers here. The lock blinked red once, then went dark.
end:0.cnHint: 我走到夜市地下通道的____，发现了一扇上锁的铁门。
end:0.hook: Behind that door, something was still breathing.
end:0.line: Grey Crow: 'Wait at the *end* of the tunnel — do not open anything yet.'

important:0.en: Ali spread the stolen data chips across the wet food stall counter. Most were trash — junk feeds, expired maps. But one chip glowed faint blue. 'This one is *important*,' Ali said, voice low. Around us, vendors kept shouting prices, unaware that the chip held Zero's entire communication network.
important:0.cnHint: 阿里在夜市摊位上发现了一块至关重要的____数据芯片。
important:0.hook: Zero's shadow moved at the far end of the market.
important:0.line: Ali: 'This chip is *important* — it maps every node Zero controls.'

cause:0.en: The food stall's signal jammer flickered on and off. Each flicker was a *cause* of dropped connections across three city blocks. Grey Crow traced the pattern on a napkin and looked up. 'Someone is doing this on purpose,' he said. My earpiece crackled once, then delivered a message I was not expecting.
cause:0.cnHint: 夜市中信号干扰仪的每次闪烁都是通讯中断的____。
cause:0.hook: The message contained only my real name.
cause:0.line: Grey Crow: 'Find the *cause* of those flickers before Zero does.'

accord:0.en: Ali slid a folded paper across the ramen counter. It was a three-point *accord* between two rival signal gangs, signed in cipher. Both sides agreed to stay out of the market tonight. 'Then why is everyone armed?' I asked. Ali said nothing. The steam from the soup curled upward like a question mark.
accord:0.cnHint: 阿里带来了两个信号帮派之间的一份____，但夜市里的人却都带着武器。
accord:0.hook: One signature on the accord was dated tomorrow.
accord:0.line: Ali: 'The *accord* says no moves tonight — someone already broke it.'

result:0.en: Grey Crow ran the decryption twice. The *result* was the same both times: the broadcast had originated from inside the night market, not the docks. He set the device down, jaw tight. I looked around at the cheerful lanterns and sizzling skewers. Somewhere among these ordinary stalls, a hidden transmitter was still running.
result:0.cnHint: 解密的____显示，神秘广播来自夜市内部而非码头。
result:0.hook: The transmitter's signal was getting stronger by the minute.
result:0.line: Grey Crow: 'The *result* points here — the source is somewhere in this market.'

recent:0.en: The vendor handed me a bowl of soup without meeting my eyes. On the bottom of the bowl, scratched into the ceramic, was a list of *recent* signal blackouts — dates, grid codes, duration. Someone had been tracking the outages for weeks and leaving the records here, hidden in plain sight, one bowl at a time.
recent:0.cnHint: 碗底刻着一份关于____信号中断事件的记录，藏在夜市的汤碗里。
recent:0.hook: The last date on the list was tonight.
recent:0.line: Ali: 'These *recent* blackouts follow a pattern — Grey Crow needs to see this.'

start:0.en: Zero's voice cut through my earpiece, calm and cold. 'You want to know how this began? I will tell you.' The *start* of it all was a single leaked frequency, three years ago, in this very market. A child had found a signal chip and broadcast it on a toy radio. Zero had been listening.
start:0.cnHint: 零点向我透露了这一切____的秘密，竟与三年前夜市里的一个孩子有关。
start:0.hook: That child, Zero said, was someone I already knew.
start:0.line: Zero: 'You think you understand the *start* — you have missed the real first move.'

however:0.en: The night market looked calm from the entrance — bright lights, loud laughter, the smell of grilled squid. *However*, every vendor I passed wore the same small earpiece, tuned to the same silent channel. Ali touched my arm. 'They are all listening for one word,' she said quietly. 'When it comes, the whole market shuts down.'
however:0.cnHint: 夜市表面热闹，____每个摊贩都戴着耳机，等待同一个暗号。
however:0.hook: Ali's own earpiece lit up before she finished speaking.
however:0.line: Ali: '*However* calm it looks, every person here is waiting for a signal.'

likely:0.en: The night market hummed with a thousand small lights. Grey Crow pulled me into a back stall selling old data chips. 'That vendor,' he whispered, nodding at a hooded figure, 'is *likely* one of Zero's watchers. See how he never buys anything?' I kept my eyes down and said nothing.
likely:0.cnHint: 灰鸦在夜市的小摊前提醒我，那个从不购物的摊贩____是零点的眼线。
likely:0.hook: The hooded figure slowly turned its face toward us.
likely:0.line: 'He is *likely* watching every newcomer who enters this row.'

experience:0.en: Ali had worked the harbor stalls for six years. Her *experience* showed in the way she read crowds — a glance told her who carried hidden goods, who was lost, who was running. She grabbed my sleeve and steered me past a checkpoint without a word. I did not ask how she knew.
experience:0.cnHint: 阿栗凭借丰富的____，一眼识破人群中的危险，悄悄带我避开了检查站。
experience:0.hook: Behind us, a checkpoint guard raised his scanner and frowned.
experience:0.line: 'My *experience* here means I know which faces to trust.'

lot:0.en: The back room of the market stall was stacked floor to ceiling with sealed crates. 'A *lot* of these boxes never get opened,' Grey Crow said quietly, tapping one with a finger. A faint signal pulsed from inside — coded, rhythmic, deliberate. Someone was broadcasting from within the crates.
lot:0.cnHint: 灰鸦发现夜市仓库里____从未开封的箱子，其中竟藏着神秘信号。
lot:0.hook: The pulse grew faster the moment I stepped closer.
lot:0.line: 'There is a *lot* here that the market owner cannot explain.'

public:0.en: A screen above the noodle stall flickered and cut to a city broadcast. Zero's distorted voice filled the *public* channel, calm and cold: 'Harbor City, your secrets are already mine.' Vendors froze. Customers stared. Ali leaned close to my ear: 'He wants everyone to hear that. Why now?'
public:0.cnHint: 零点突然占据了____频道，向整个夜市播报令人不安的消息。
public:0.hook: Every screen in the market switched to the same blank white feed.
public:0.line: 'He chose a *public* channel so no one could claim they never heard it.'

example:0.en: Grey Crow set a cracked data chip on the counter between us. 'Look at this,' he said. 'It is an *example* of Zero's early code — simple, almost playful. But every later attack grew from this same root.' I studied the tiny lines etched on its surface and felt a chill.
example:0.cnHint: 灰鸦展示了一块旧芯片，称它是理解零点编程风格的____。
example:0.hook: One line of the etched code matched the signal I had heard an hour ago.
example:0.line: 'This chip is an *example* of how Zero first learned to hide messages.'

whether:0.en: Ali pressed a folded slip into my hand without looking at me. On it were two addresses. 'Decide fast,' she murmured, eyes on the crowd. '*Whether* you go to the port or the signal tower, you have ten minutes before the grid locks down.' I stared at both addresses and breathed slowly.
whether:0.cnHint: 阿栗递给我两个地址，让我迅速决定____去港口还是信号塔。
whether:0.hook: Somewhere above us, the city grid gave a low, warning hum.
whether:0.line: '*Whether* you trust me or not, you must choose before the bell rings.'

focus:0.en: The noise of the market — voices, frying oil, distant music — fell away as I stared at the chip reader. Grey Crow touched my shoulder. 'Keep your *focus*,' he said. 'Zero plants distractions everywhere. The real signal is always the quiet one.' I slowed my breath and looked again at the screen.
focus:0.cnHint: 灰鸦提醒我在嘈杂的夜市中保持____，不要被零点设置的干扰迷惑。
focus:0.hook: The quiet signal on the screen suddenly blinked and vanished.
focus:0.line: 'Keep your *focus* on the data, not on the noise around you.'

avoid:0.en: The market's main aisle was bright and watched. Grey Crow took a sharp turn into a side passage stacked with empty crates. 'We *avoid* the center,' he said, not slowing down. 'Zero's watchers cluster where the lights are strongest.' The passage was dark and smelled of salt water and old wiring.
avoid:0.cnHint: 灰鸦带我绕开人流密集的主通道，以____零点在灯光最亮处设置的眼线。
avoid:0.hook: At the far end of the dark passage, a shadow moved.
avoid:0.line: 'We *avoid* the bright aisles — that is where they count faces.'

actually:0.en: The night market hummed with stolen signals. Grey Crow pulled me into a dim tea stall and pressed a small device into my hand. 'This reads coded broadcasts,' he said. I switched it on. The chatter all around us was *actually* a live feed of encrypted police orders — disguised as vendor calls.
actually:0.cnHint: 茶馆里嘈杂的叫卖声____是加密的警务指令。
actually:0.hook: One vendor's eyes locked onto mine and did not look away.
actually:0.line: 'What you hear *actually* decides whether we walk out of here.'

themselves:0.en: I watched the food-stall owners move through the crowded indoor market with strange calm. Ali leaned close and whispered that they had trained *themselves* to ignore the surveillance drones overhead — every gesture rehearsed, every word measured. Survival in Harbor City wore the mask of ordinary life.
themselves:0.cnHint: 摊主们____训练成对无人机视而不见。
themselves:0.hook: Then one of them dropped the mask and stared straight at me.
themselves:0.line: 'They taught *themselves* to look innocent — and that is exactly what worries me.'

person:0.en: A single *person* stood still inside the rushing night market crowd — no food, no device, no apparent reason to be there. Ali grabbed my arm. Grey Crow had warned us: a stationary figure in a moving crowd was never lost. They were always waiting. For something. Or someone.
person:0.cnHint: 人群中一个静止不动的____引起了我们的警觉。
person:0.hook: The person's lips moved, but the words reached no one — except my receiver.
person:0.line: 'Every *person* in this market has a role — what is that one playing?'

without:0.en: The indoor signal hub was buried beneath a noodle shop. Zero had been there before us — wires cut cleanly, logs erased, the room left *without* a single trace of who had operated it. I ran my fingers along the cold rack. One chip was still warm.
without:0.cnHint: 信号站被彻底清空，____留下任何痕迹。
without:0.hook: Warm metal meant Zero had left less than three minutes ago.
without:0.line: 'A room *without* evidence is the loudest kind of confession.'

among:0.en: Grey Crow spread a map of the market stalls across a back table. Hidden relay points were marked in faint ink. *Among* them, one was circled twice — a fish vendor near the east wall. 'That is where the next broadcast originates,' he said, tapping the circle with one finger.
among:0.cnHint: 所有中继点____，有一个被标记了两次。
among:0.hook: The fish vendor's stall had already gone dark when we arrived.
among:0.line: '*Among* all these points, only one is live tonight — find it fast.'

suppose:0.en: Ali handed me a cracked data chip. 'I *suppose* this is what Zero dropped on the way out,' she said, voice flat. The chip was warm and still active. Whatever was on it had not finished transmitting. I looked around the narrow indoor corridor. We were not alone in it.
suppose:0.cnHint: 阿栗____这块芯片是零点仓皇逃走时落下的。
suppose:0.hook: The chip beeped once — and the lights in the corridor died.
suppose:0.line: 'I *suppose* you have a plan for what we do if that chip calls someone back.'

health:0.en: The black-market clinic was tucked inside the market's back wing, behind a row of spice counters. A sign read GENERAL *HEALTH* CHECKS, but Grey Crow said every patient who entered left carrying a coded message stitched into their discharge slip. Medicine was just the cover story tonight.
health:0.cnHint: 这家打着____检查幌子的诊所其实是传递密信的据点。
health:0.hook: The next patient on the list was booked under my name.
health:0.line: 'They use *health* records as drop boxes — yours was accessed an hour ago.'

mean:0.en: Zero left a single word sprayed on the clinic wall: LISTEN. Ali said it could *mean* a warning, a taunt, or a command — she could not decide which. I raised my receiver. A tight-beam signal pulsed from somewhere inside the building, steady and patient, as if it had been waiting just for me.
mean:0.cnHint: 墙上那个词究竟____什么，我们谁也说不准。
mean:0.hook: The signal carried a voice — and the voice was mine.
mean:0.line: 'One word can *mean* everything or nothing — Zero knows exactly which.'

view:0.en: The signal came from inside the Night Market's old radio shop. Grey Crow pressed a worn map against the glass and said nothing. I studied every mark on it, trying to *view* the city the way a ghost would — from above, from the cracks, from the silence between broadcasts.
view:0.cnHint: 在旧无线电铺里，灰鸦用一张地图教我用新的____来理解这座城市。
view:0.hook: One mark on the map had no name — only a blinking dot.
view:0.line: '*View* the city like a ghost, and you will find what others miss.'

social:0.en: The back room of the noodle stall smelled of burnt wire and cheap soup. Ali spread a chart on the table — a web of names, faces, debts. 'This is their *social* network,' she said. Every node was a person. Every line was a secret. Two nodes had already gone dark.
social:0.cnHint: 阿里在摊位后间展示了一张____网络图，其中两个节点已经消失。
social:0.hook: The third node began to blink — it was my name.
social:0.line: 'Their *social* network looks friendly, but every link hides a trap.'

skill:0.en: Zero sat at the counter of the closed tea house, cracking encrypted tokens with bare fingers on a dead keyboard. No screen. No sound. Just muscle memory. I had never seen *skill* like that — cold, clean, and a little frightening. He did not look up once.
skill:0.cnHint: 在废弃茶馆里，零点展示了令人不安的解密____。
skill:0.hook: He slid one cracked token across the counter — it had my access code.
skill:0.line: 'Raw *skill* with no purpose is just a loaded weapon waiting to fire.'

job:0.en: Grey Crow found me in the back corridor of the market's closed print shop, surrounded by stacked paper and old ink. He handed me a folded card with a single address on it. 'Your *job* is not to arrest anyone tonight,' he said. 'Your job is to listen.'
job:0.cnHint: 灰鸦在印刷店走廊里交给我一张卡片，说明了我今晚真正的____。
job:0.hook: The address on the card was my own apartment building.
job:0.line: 'Your *job* tonight is to listen — nothing more, nothing less.'

business:0.en: The market's currency exchange booth was shut, but a light moved inside. Ali pressed her ear to the thin wall. 'Somebody is still doing *business* in there,' she whispered. A shadow crossed the frosted glass. Then a second shadow. Then a third. None of them matched any face on our list.
business:0.cnHint: 阿里发现关闭的兑币亭里仍有人在做____，但那些身影无法辨认。
business:0.hook: The third shadow stopped and seemed to look straight at Ali.
business:0.line: 'Strange *business* goes on here long after the shutters come down.'

eat:0.en: We ducked into a narrow canteen behind the fish stalls. I ordered something hot and tried to *eat* fast, but Grey Crow touched my arm. 'Slow down,' he said quietly. 'The man in the corner has been watching your bowl, not his own.' I set the chopsticks down and did not look up.
eat:0.cnHint: 在市场深处的小食堂里，我试图____东西，却察觉到有人在盯着我们。
eat:0.hook: The man in the corner stood up before we finished.
eat:0.line: 'If you *eat* like you are running, they will know you are afraid.'

healthy:0.en: The herbal medicine stall was locked, but its window display still glowed. Rows of bright roots and dried leaves, each tagged with a price and a promise. Ali read one label aloud: *healthy* body, quiet mind. 'That is what Zero wants from this city,' she said. 'Everything quiet. Everything still.'
healthy:0.cnHint: 草药摊的橱窗里，阿里从一张标签上读出了零点对这座城市的____野心。
healthy:0.hook: Behind the roots, a small camera blinked green — it was live.
healthy:0.line: 'A *healthy* city, Zero calls it — but only the obedient ones survive.'

place:0.en: The map led us to a storage room beneath the market's main floor — no sign, no number, just a rusted door. Grey Crow said this *place* had once been used to hide radio parts during the signal blackout of 2087. The air still smelled of old metal and dried static.
place:0.cnHint: 地图把我们引到了市场地下一个曾被用来藏匿无线电零件的____。
place:0.hook: The rusted door was already open — from the inside.
place:0.line: 'This *place* remembers every secret that was ever buried here.'

less:1.en: The night market blazed with color, but I felt *less* safe with every step. Grey Crow had warned me: the stalls here were fronts. Behind the steam and noise, watchers tracked every stranger. I kept my hood up and my eyes down, moving like I belonged.
less:1.cnHint: 我在夜市中感到____安全，灰鸦曾警告过我这里暗藏监视。
less:1.hook: One watcher peeled away from the crowd and followed me.
less:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'Trust *less*, move faster — that is the only rule here.'

information:1.en: Ali pressed a folded paper into my palm without looking at me. 'Old method,' she murmured. The paper held raw *information*: names, stall numbers, pickup times. In Harbor City, data on paper was invisible to the grid. I read it once, then let the rain dissolve it.
information:1.cnHint: 阿里悄悄递给我一张纸，上面写着关键____。
information:1.hook: The last name on the list was mine.
information:1.line: Ali whispered, '*Information* on paper leaves no signal — read it and let it go.'

paragraph:1.en: On the wall beside a noodle stall, someone had sprayed a single *paragraph* of white text. It looked like a food ad, but I had been trained to read the second layer. Every fifth word was a coordinate. Grey Crow had taught me this code. I snapped a photo fast.
paragraph:1.cnHint: 夜市墙上的一____涂鸦藏着隐秘坐标，我迅速拍下。
paragraph:1.hook: A light above the wall clicked on, and a camera swung my way.
paragraph:1.line: Grey Crow told me, 'Read the *paragraph* twice — the real message hides in the gaps.'

look:1.en: I stopped at a fish stall and gave the vendor a slow *look* — the kind that said I was browsing, nothing more. He returned it with a slight nod. That nod meant the drop was ready. Ali had set this up. The package sat under a pile of crushed ice.
look:1.cnHint: 我用特定的____示意摊主，确认接头暗号成立。
look:1.hook: Then a second vendor appeared and blocked my path.
look:1.line: 'Give me that *look* one more time,' the vendor said, 'so I know it is really you.'

benefit:1.en: Zero operated in the market openly. That was his style, his *benefit*: hide in plain sight. He sold signal jammers labeled as kitchen timers. No one questioned a vendor. I watched him from across the lane, logging his contacts. He had three in ten minutes.
benefit:1.cnHint: 零点把公开现身当作自己的____，在人群中光明正大地行动。
benefit:1.hook: Then Zero looked up and smiled directly at me.
benefit:1.line: Zero said, 'The *benefit* of selling in the open is that no one thinks to look.'

contain:1.en: The small metal box Ali had left under the third bench could *contain* no more than a deck of cards, but its weight told a different story. I did not open it in the market. Around me, shoppers pushed close. I tucked the box inside my coat and kept walking.
contain:1.cnHint: 阿里留下的小金属盒能____的东西有限，但分量却令人生疑。
contain:1.hook: Something inside the box shifted when I turned the corner.
contain:1.line: Ali's voice came through my earpiece: 'What it can *contain* matters less than what it must not lose.'

direction:1.en: The market stretched in four directions from the central fountain. Grey Crow had given me no map, only a rule: follow the smell of burnt wire. It was strange *direction*, but in Harbor City the old cables leaked heat in patterns only the trained could read. I found the smell fast.
direction:1.cnHint: 灰鸦给了我奇特的____——跟着焦线的气味走。
direction:1.hook: The smell led me straight to a door that should not exist.
direction:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'When the grid lies, let your nose give you *direction*.'

attach:1.en: Zero's courier paused at a lamp post, pretending to check his shoe. In that second he managed to *attach* a thin strip of film to the post's base. Coded light patterns, Grey Crow had said. I photographed the strip before the courier stood up and vanished into the crowd.
attach:1.cnHint: 零点的信使趁人不注意，将一条薄膜____在灯柱底部。
attach:1.hook: The film strip began to blink once, then went dark forever.
attach:1.line: '*Attach* it low,' Zero had said, 'and the city's eyes will never look down that far.'

end:1.en: The night market stretched along the old pier. I walked its full length, past smoking food carts and blinking signs, until I reached the *end* of the road — a rusted gate, padlocked, with a single red light blinking behind it.
end:1.cnHint: 我走到夜市的____，发现了一扇锁着的铁门和诡异的红光。
end:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'The answer waits at the *end* of the line.'

important:1.en: Ali pulled me aside between two stalls selling fried dough. 'This spot,' she whispered, eyes cutting left and right, 'is *important*. Every coded message in Harbor City passes through here — in the steam, in the noise, in the grease-stained paper bags.' I looked around. It felt like any other stall.
important:1.cnHint: 阿栗告诉我这个摊位非常____，是情报传递的关键节点。
important:1.hook: Then I saw the ink mark on the bag.
important:1.line: Ali said, 'You have no idea how *important* this corner is.'

cause:1.en: A power cut turned the whole block dark. Grey Crow did not even blink. 'A small signal burst can *cause* a blackout this size,' he said, scanning the crowd. 'Someone nearby just sent a message they did not want recorded.' The lights came back. One face in the crowd was already gone.
cause:1.cnHint: 一次信号爆发____了整片区域停电，灰鸦立刻意识到有人在传递秘密。
cause:1.hook: The empty space in the crowd told us everything.
cause:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'A single burst can *cause* a blackout this wide.'

accord:1.en: Zero appeared beside my shoulder without a sound. He slid a folded slip into my hand and said nothing. The numbers on it were in perfect *accord* with the coded map Ali had drawn last night — same grid, same marks, same sequence. That could not be chance. Zero was either helping us or setting a trap.
accord:1.cnHint: 零点给我的纸条与阿栗的地图完全____，这让我无法判断他是盟友还是敌人。
accord:1.hook: Zero was already gone before I looked up.
accord:1.line: Zero said, 'My data and yours are in *accord*. Think about that.'

result:1.en: I replayed the broadcast twice through my earpiece. The hidden syllables, once sorted, gave a clear *result*: a warehouse number and a tide time. Ali had said decoding it would take days. It had taken me twenty minutes. Either I was lucky, or the message had been left easy on purpose.
result:1.cnHint: 解码广播的____令我震惊——难道这个线索是故意留给我的？
result:1.hook: Someone wanted me to find that warehouse tonight.
result:1.line: Ali said, 'Tell me the *result* and we move in ten minutes.'

recent:1.en: The graffiti covered the whole east wall of the market. Most of it was old, flaking, harmless. But one tag was *recent* — the paint still slightly wet under my fingertip. It was the same spiral symbol I had seen in three other locations this week. Someone was drawing a map right in front of everyone.
recent:1.cnHint: 墙上有一处____的涂鸦，颜料未干，与本周其他地点的符号完全相同。
recent:1.hook: The spiral pointed directly toward the old dock.
recent:1.line: Grey Crow said, 'This tag is *recent*. They were here tonight.'

start:1.en: Ali crouched over a small drain at the market entrance, torch in hand. 'Every signal trail has to *start* somewhere,' she said. 'This drain runs under four city blocks and comes up inside the building we want.' She looked up at me. Rain began to fall. 'You first,' she said.
start:1.cnHint: 阿栗发现每条信号追踪都有一个____点，而这个排水口正是关键入口。
start:1.hook: The drain was just wide enough for one person.
start:1.line: Ali said, 'Every trail has to *start* from a single point.'

however:1.en: The market noise was deafening — drums, frying oil, a hundred voices. Zero had assured me the drop would happen at midnight. Midnight passed. *However*, at 00:07, a green paper bag changed hands three stalls down, quick as a blink. Seven minutes late. Zero never made mistakes. Seven minutes was a message in itself.
however:1.cnHint: 零点说好午夜交接，____时间稍有偏差，我意识到这七分钟本身就是一条线索。
however:1.hook: I already knew what seven minutes meant in their code.
however:1.line: Zero said, '*However* late I am, the number still counts.'

human:1.en: The night market blazed with cheap neon. Smoke from a hundred food stalls burned my eyes. I watched the crowd and felt something wrong — the figures near the east gate moved too perfectly, too still between steps. No *human* moves like that. Grey Crow's voice crackled in my ear: 'Don't look twice.'
human:1.cnHint: 我在夜市人群中发现，东门附近的几个身影移动方式不像____所为。
human:1.hook: One of them slowly turned its face toward me.
human:1.line: 'A real *human* would have blinked by now,' Grey Crow whispered.

large:1.en: Ali pulled me behind a fish stall and pointed up. A *large* screen on the market tower was running a city-safety broadcast, but underneath the official words, coded graffiti flickered — just for a second — spelling out a grid address. Someone had hacked the signal. The vendor beside us pretended not to see.
large:1.cnHint: 阿栗发现夜市高塔上那块____的屏幕被人植入了一段隐藏信息。
large:1.hook: The grid address pointed straight to the old port warehouse.
large:1.line: 'That *large* screen just told us exactly where to go,' Ali said.

likely:1.en: The night market blazed with color, but I kept my eyes on the shadows. Grey Crow had warned me: 'Watch the ones who never buy anything.' Across three stalls, the same figure appeared — hood up, hands empty. He was *likely* our contact, or our problem.
likely:1.cnHint: 夜市人潮中，调查员注意到一个从不购物的可疑身影，灰鸦说这人____是线人，也可能是麻烦。
likely:1.hook: The figure turned, and our eyes locked.
likely:1.line: 'He is *likely* the one Zero sent to watch us.'

experience:1.en: Rain drummed the market's tin roofs as Ali handed me a steaming bowl. 'First time in Harbor City?' she asked. I nodded. She smiled, sharp and quick. 'Your *experience* here will change you — the city reads you before you read it.' She wasn't wrong. Something already felt off.
experience:1.cnHint: 阿栗告诉调查员，在这座城市的____会彻底改变一个人，而此刻调查员已感到有些不对劲。
experience:1.hook: Behind Ali, a coded sign on the wall began to blink.
experience:1.line: 'Your *experience* in this city will teach you things no school can.'

lot:1.en: Grey Crow moved fast through the crowded stalls, and I followed close. 'Zero has a *lot* of eyes here,' he said without turning. I looked around — vendors, children, an old man reading a screen. Any one of them could be listening. The market felt less like a street, more like a trap.
lot:1.cnHint: 灰鸦警告调查员，零点在夜市安插了____眼线，整条街都可能是陷阱。
lot:1.hook: Then Grey Crow stopped cold and raised one fist.
lot:1.line: 'Zero has a *lot* of people watching this block tonight.'

public:1.en: A broadcast crackled from a speaker above the fish stalls. Official words, clean and smooth. But under the noise I caught a second signal — short, sharp, coded. Grey Crow leaned in: 'That *public* message is just the cover. The real order is underneath it.' My hand went to my recorder.
public:1.cnHint: 夜市广播中，官方____消息只是掩护，灰鸦说真正的指令藏在信号底层。
public:1.hook: The coded signal cut off before I could finish recording.
public:1.line: 'The *public* broadcast is a mask — the real message is hidden inside it.'

example:1.en: Ali pointed to a wall of graffiti near the food stalls. Each tag looked random, but she traced one with her finger. 'This *example* — see the double loop? It means a drop point changed.' I stared. The whole wall was a map. Anyone walking past would see only color and noise.
example:1.cnHint: 阿栗指着涂鸦墙向调查员解释，这个____标记代表接头地点已经更换。
example:1.hook: Someone had painted a fresh tag over the very one she pointed at.
example:1.line: 'This *example* on the wall tells us Zero moved the drop point.'

whether:1.en: My earpiece crackled. Grey Crow's voice was low and flat: 'You need to decide now — *whether* you trust the map Ali gave you, or you walk away clean.' The market noise pressed in from all sides. I looked at the folded paper in my hand. One path forward. One way back.
whether:1.cnHint: 灰鸦逼调查员立刻决定，____相信阿栗给的地图，决定将改变一切。
whether:1.hook: I unfolded the map — and found a second message beneath it.
whether:1.line: '*Whether* you trust her or not, you have thirty seconds to choose.'

focus:1.en: Noise hit me from every direction — voices, music, the sizzle of street food. I was losing track of the target. Ali grabbed my arm: 'Drop all that. Your *focus* needs to be on the blue stall, third row.' I steadied my breath and looked. The vendor there was packing up too fast.
focus:1.cnHint: 阿栗提醒调查员把____放在第三排蓝色摊位，那个摊主收摊的速度不同寻常。
focus:1.hook: The vendor tucked something small and flat beneath his coat.
focus:1.line: 'Your *focus* should be on that blue stall — nothing else matters now.'

avoid:1.en: Grey Crow steered me left without a word, away from the main path. 'We *avoid* the central crossing,' he said quietly. 'Zero's people check bags there — random, they say.' I glanced back. Two figures in gray coats stood at the crossing, watching every face that passed beneath the red lights.
avoid:1.cnHint: 灰鸦带调查员绕路，目的是____中央路口处零点手下的例行检查。
avoid:1.hook: One of the gray coats turned and pointed — directly at us.
avoid:1.line: 'We *avoid* that crossing, or we hand ourselves to Zero tonight.'

view:1.en: The night market stretched along the wet dock, steam rising from a hundred stalls. Grey Crow pulled me close and said nothing — just pointed. From the roof edge, the *view* of Harbor City opened like a wound: neon signs bleeding into black water, coded signals flashing in every window.
view:1.cnHint: 格雷·克劳带我站上屋顶，Harbor City的____让我第一次意识到这座城市藏着多少秘密。
view:1.hook: Every blinking light was a message — but for whom?
view:1.line: 'Take in the *view* — the signals are hidden inside it,' Grey Crow said.

social:1.en: The market was loud and packed. Ali moved through the crowd like water, stopping at every stall, laughing, touching shoulders. 'That is her *social* skill,' Grey Crow murmured beside me. 'Every vendor trusts her. Every vendor talks.' I watched her collect secrets with a smile and a bowl of noodles.
social:1.cnHint: 阿栗在夜市里游刃有余，她的____能力让每个摊主都愿意开口。
social:1.hook: She laughed at the last stall — then her face went still.
social:1.line: 'In this city, your *social* game is your only armor,' Ali said.

skill:1.en: Zero appeared at the edge of the market, fingers moving fast over a small device. Grey Crow tensed. 'Watch that,' he said quietly. Zero's *skill* with a code-breaker was famous — three encrypted walls cracked in under a minute. The market noise died in my ears. He was already inside our signal.
skill:1.cnHint: 零点展示了他破解加密信号的____，让我们意识到情况比预想的更危险。
skill:1.hook: The device blinked green — our private channel was open to him.
skill:1.line: 'Raw *skill* opened that lock. No key needed,' Zero said coldly.

job:1.en: Ali pressed a food ticket into my hand and leaned close. 'Your *job* tonight is simple,' she whispered. 'Walk the east row, buy something at every third stall, and listen.' Simple words. But the way her eyes moved told me the east row was being watched. I took the ticket and walked.
job:1.cnHint: 阿栗交代了我今晚的____：沿着东排摊位走，边买东西边收集情报。
job:1.hook: At the seventh stall, the vendor did not look up once.
job:1.line: 'Do the *job* clean and quiet — no questions asked,' Ali said.

business:1.en: A stall near the water sold encrypted paper maps — old tech, hard to trace. The owner, a thin man with ink-stained hands, watched me without blinking. 'You are not here for food,' he said. Grey Crow stepped forward. 'We are here for *business*,' he said. The man slid a map across the wet counter.
business:1.cnHint: 格雷·克劳在一个隐秘摊位前开口谈____，摊主随即推来一张神秘地图。
business:1.hook: The map showed a building that no longer existed — officially.
business:1.line: 'Keep your *business* clean and no one asks questions,' Grey Crow said.

eat:1.en: The smell of hot broth pulled me toward a corner stall. Ali caught my arm. 'Not that one.' I looked closer — the customers there did not *eat*. They held bowls and stared ahead, earpieces barely hidden under their collars. Every stall in the row was a post. The market was a trap dressed as dinner.
eat:1.cnHint: 我想去角落的摊位，但阿栗拦住了我——那些假装____的人其实是监视者。
eat:1.hook: One of them turned slowly — and looked straight at me.
eat:1.line: 'Don't *eat* there — those people are not what they seem,' Ali warned.

healthy:1.en: Grey Crow bought two cups of warm grain tea and handed one to me. 'Drink,' he said. I almost laughed — it felt strange to care about something *healthy* in a city built on poison signals and coded lies. But the warmth in my chest was real. 'Stay sharp,' he added. 'Tonight is long.'
healthy:1.cnHint: 格雷·克劳递给我一杯热茶，在这座危机四伏的城市里，这点____的小事反而让我安心。
healthy:1.hook: Then his earpiece crackled and his expression went flat.
healthy:1.line: 'Stay *healthy* — a sharp mind starts with a warm body,' Grey Crow said.

place:1.en: Ali stopped walking and looked around slowly. 'This is the *place*,' she said. A gap between two stalls, unmarked, no light. The vendors on each side kept their backs turned — too carefully. Beneath the smell of grilled food, something electric hummed. A relay node, hidden in plain sight, powering every coded broadcast in the market.
place:1.cnHint: 阿栗找到了那个关键的____，就藏在两个摊位之间，伪装成毫不起眼的角落。
place:1.hook: Someone had already been here — the panel was warm to the touch.
place:1.line: 'This *place* is the heart of every signal tonight,' Ali said quietly.

actually:1.en: The night market blazed with a thousand lights, but I was not here for the food. I was tracking a signal. Grey Crow had told me the source was a vendor. But the stall was empty — the vendor had *actually* vanished, leaving only a burning lantern and a single folded note.
actually:1.cnHint: 我在夜市追踪信号源，才发现摊主____已经消失，只留下一盏灯和一张纸条。
actually:1.hook: The note held three words: 'They heard you.'
actually:1.line: 'The vendor *actually* left ten seconds before you arrived,' Grey Crow said.

themselves:1.en: Near the spice stalls, I spotted two figures in grey coats. They moved in tight circles, speaking to no one else. The crowd parted around them like water around stone. Those two had wrapped *themselves* in silence, and every vendor nearby had turned their backs. Something was wrong here.
themselves:1.cnHint: 夜市中，两个灰衣人把____裹在沉默里，周围所有摊贩都背过身去。
themselves:1.hook: Then one of them looked directly at my hidden camera.
themselves:1.line: 'They kept *themselves* hidden for three hours,' Ali whispered into my earpiece.

person:1.en: Ali sent me a photo: one *person* standing at the far end of the market, half in shadow, holding a device no bigger than a coin. The crowd moved around this figure but never touched them. I had seen that coat before — last winter, at the coded-graffiti wall. My pulse jumped.
person:1.cnHint: 阿栗发来一张照片，夜市尽头有一个____，手持神秘装置，独自站在阴影里。
person:1.hook: My own face appeared on the device's small screen.
person:1.line: 'There is only one *person* in this city who uses that frequency,' Grey Crow said flatly.

without:1.en: I moved through the crowded stalls, past sizzling skewers and glowing lanterns. Zero was ahead — I was sure of it. I followed the signal pulse and reached the corner *without* making a sound. A black case sat open on the wet ground. It was empty. Zero had already been here and gone.
without:1.cnHint: 我悄悄穿过夜市，____发出任何声音就追到了角落，却发现零点已经离开。
without:1.hook: A second pulse began — and it came from behind me.
without:1.line: 'You walked right past the case *without* seeing it,' Zero's voice crackled on my radio.

among:1.en: Grey Crow told me the stolen data chip was hidden somewhere in the night market. I scanned every stall, every crate, every shadow. Then I saw it — a faint blue light blinking *among* the red paper lanterns above the noodle stand. Hidden in plain sight, thirty feet above the wet street.
among:1.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉我芯片就藏在夜市里，我终于在红灯笼____发现了一个蓝色闪光。
among:1.hook: My hand reached up — and the light went dark.
among:1.line: 'It has been *among* those lanterns since midnight,' Grey Crow said quietly.

suppose:1.en: The market vendor slid a bowl of tea toward me without a word. I had not ordered it. I looked around for Grey Crow but saw only strangers. I *suppose* someone had told her I would come here tonight — but only Ali knew my route. I stared at the bowl and did not drink.
suppose:1.cnHint: 摊贩无声地递来一碗茶，我____是有人提前通知了她，但只有阿栗知道我的路线。
suppose:1.hook: At the bowl's bottom, a tiny data chip glinted.
suppose:1.line: 'I *suppose* you already know who sent that tea,' Ali said, her voice tight.

health:1.en: The signal led me to a small stall selling herbal drinks. A sign read: 'Good *health* starts with clean air.' Below it, in tiny coded script, was a message only I could read. It listed four names. Mine was third. My hands stayed steady but my mind was already running through exits.
health:1.cnHint: 信号把我引到一个草药摊，招牌上写着____从干净的空气开始，下方却藏着一条密语。
health:1.hook: The fourth name on the list had already been crossed out.
health:1.line: 'They use the word *health* as a code for their next target,' Grey Crow said.

mean:1.en: Zero stepped out from behind a silk curtain at the edge of the market. 'You followed the lantern,' Zero said. 'What do you think that *means*?' I said nothing. In this city, a blinking light could mean a warning, a trap, or a hand reaching out. I had not decided which one yet.
mean:1.cnHint: 零点走出幕后，问我追踪灯光____着什么，而我还没想清楚答案。
mean:1.hook: Zero smiled — and the market lights cut to black.
mean:1.line: 'Every coded sign here *means* something, if you know how to look,' Zero said.

derive:1.en: The night market hummed with stolen frequencies. Grey Crow pressed a small device to the wet iron post. 'You can *derive* power from the city's own signal grid,' he said. The device lit up green. Somewhere above, a hidden antenna began to turn.
derive:1.cnHint: 灰鸦教我如何从城市信号网络中____电力，装置随即亮起绿光。
derive:1.hook: The antenna's signal pointed straight at Zero's last known location.
derive:1.line: 'You can *derive* power from the city's own signal grid.'

report:1.en: Ali slapped a crumpled sheet on the food stall counter. 'This *report* puts three blackout zones on the harbor map,' she said. Rain blurred the ink at the edges. The vendor froze, eyes on the paper, then slowly reached under the counter with one hand.
report:1.cnHint: 阿栗带来了一份关于港口停电区域的____，摊贩的反应却令人起疑。
report:1.hook: His other hand was already tapping a silent warning to someone.
report:1.line: 'This *report* puts three blackout zones on the harbor map.'

research:1.en: Grey Crow found me crouched behind a noodle cart. 'Your *research* into the coded graffiti is too close to the truth,' he said quietly. Around us, the market crowd moved without looking up. A red drone hovered one block away, its camera lens locked on our position.
research:1.cnHint: 灰鸦警告我，对涂鸦密码的____已经触碰到了危险的真相。
research:1.hook: The drone began drifting closer, inch by inch.
research:1.line: 'Your *research* into the coded graffiti is too close to the truth.'

different:1.en: The graffiti on the east wall looked *different* tonight — new lines cut across the old pattern. Ali traced the edges with one finger. 'Someone rewrote the code after midnight,' she said. The market lights flickered once, then died, leaving only the cold glow of her scanner.
different:1.cnHint: 东墙上的涂鸦今晚变得____了，阿栗发现有人在午夜后篡改了密码。
different:1.hook: In the darkness, a second set of footsteps matched our own exactly.
different:1.line: 'Someone rewrote the code, the whole pattern is *different* now.'

author:1.en: A name surfaced in the signal stream: the *author* of Harbor City's master encryption key. Grey Crow read it twice and said nothing. Ali looked at me, jaw tight. The name belonged to someone we had trusted for months, someone still buying fish at the stall three meters away.
author:1.cnHint: 信号流中浮现出主加密密钥____的名字，那是一个我们曾信任的人。
author:1.hook: He turned and smiled, as if he had heard every word.
author:1.line: 'We finally know the *author* of the master key.'

increase:1.en: 'The encrypted broadcasts show a sharp *increase* over the last six hours,' Ali said, tapping her wrist screen. Market noise covered her voice, but not well enough. A man selling cold drinks tilted his head half a degree. His lips did not move, but his earpiece blinked twice.
increase:1.cnHint: 阿栗发现加密广播数量急剧____，但附近有人似乎也在监听这段对话。
increase:1.hook: The drink seller set down his cart and walked toward the east exit.
increase:1.line: 'The data shows a sharp *increase* in encrypted broadcasts tonight.'

university:1.en: The tip said to look for a pin badge from the old Harbor *university* — dissolved in 2047, its records wiped. Grey Crow spotted it on a food vendor's collar in the crowded night market. 'That badge is a signal,' he said. The vendor met his eyes for exactly one second.
university:1.cnHint: 线索指向一枚早已解散的____徽章，灰鸦在夜市摊贩身上发现了它。
university:1.hook: Then the vendor dropped his ladle and ran.
university:1.line: 'That badge from the old *university* — it is not just a badge.'

turn:1.en: 'Do not *turn* around,' Ali whispered from behind a steaming cart. 'Zero is ten meters back and closing.' The market crowd pressed in from both sides. I counted to three, fixed my eyes on the far canal gate, and matched the rhythm of the crowd like a moving shadow.
turn:1.cnHint: 阿栗低声警告我不要____身，因为零点就在身后步步逼近。
turn:1.hook: A hand closed around my wrist before I reached the gate.
turn:1.line: 'Do not *turn* around — Zero is right behind you.'

derive:2.en: Deep in the Harbor Night Market, I found a cracked data chip behind a noodle stall. Grey Crow said we could *derive* its origin from the signal pattern burned into it. I pressed my fingers to the chip and felt something cold — a name, almost readable.
derive:2.cnHint: 我在夜市摊位后发现一块破损芯片，灰鸦说可以从信号中____出它的来源。
derive:2.hook: The name on the chip was mine.
derive:2.line: 'We can *derive* the source — if you are ready for what it shows.'

report:2.en: Ali shoved a folded paper into my hand near the spice market. It was a *report* — three pages, dense with numbers — tracking signal spikes across Harbor City over the past week. Every spike pointed to the same block. This block. The one we were standing on.
report:2.cnHint: 阿栗递给我一份____，上面记录的信号异常全都指向我们脚下这片区域。
report:2.hook: Someone had circled my face in the margin.
report:2.line: 'This *report* came from inside the system — no one should have it.'

research:2.en: Behind a tea stall wrapped in red lanterns, Grey Crow spread out months of *research* across a wet table. Charts, coded notes, signal maps — all pointing to a hidden broadcast tower somewhere in the Night Market. The data was solid. The danger was more solid.
research:2.cnHint: 灰鸦在茶摊后展开了数月的____成果，所有线索都指向夜市里某座隐藏的信号塔。
research:2.hook: Then the lanterns all went dark at once.
research:2.line: 'My *research* ends here — your part begins now.'

different:2.en: I compared two signal prints side by side on my lens. They looked almost identical, but Zero had warned me that the second one was *different* in one small and fatal way. I found the difference buried in the last line of code. It was a trap address.
different:2.cnHint: 两份信号图看似相同，但零点警告我第二份在某处____，我在最后一行代码里找到了答案——那是一个陷阱地址。
different:2.hook: My lens cracked before I could read it fully.
different:2.line: 'Look closer — it is *different*, and that difference will kill you.'

author:2.en: The graffiti on the market wall shifted as I walked past — not paint, but light pixels, coded and alive. Grey Crow knelt and read the signature at the base. The *author* had left a single glyph, a mark I had seen before on the chip from the noodle stall.
author:2.cnHint: 墙上的像素涂鸦底部有一个签名，灰鸦说这位____留下的标记和芯片上的一模一样。
author:2.line: 'The *author* of this message is someone we both trusted.'

increase:2.en: Ali watched the crowd density map on her wrist screen. The *increase* in bodies moving toward the east gate was too regular to be natural — someone was pushing people in that direction on purpose. We had maybe four minutes before whatever was at the east gate became our problem.
increase:2.cnHint: 人群密度图显示东门方向人流____异常，阿栗判断有人在故意引导人群朝那里聚集。
increase:2.hook: My earpiece crackled — then went silent.
increase:2.line: 'This *increase* is not random — someone is herding them.'

university:2.en: The old *university* badge on the vendor's jacket caught my eye — Harbor City Tech, Class of 2041. Grey Crow had told me to look for exactly that badge. The vendor met my stare, slid a wrapped data card across the counter, and walked away without a word.
university:2.cnHint: 摊主夹克上的旧____徽章引起了我的注意，灰鸦曾叮嘱我寻找这个标志。
university:2.hook: The data card was still warm.
university:2.line: 'The *university* badge is the signal — trust no one else tonight.'

turn:2.en: Ali said to follow the blue lanterns and *turn* right at the fish market corner. I did. The alley behind was empty except for a metal box welded to the wall, its lock already broken. Inside was a folded strip of film with six frames — each one a different face. I knew two of them.
turn:2.cnHint: 按照阿栗的指示____弯进小巷后，我在墙上的金属盒里发现了一条胶片，上面有六张面孔。
turn:2.hook: One of the faces was looking straight at the camera — smiling.
turn:2.line: '*Turn* right, walk fast, and do not look back at the market.'

less:2.en: The night market hummed with a hundred voices. Ali pressed a folded note into my hand near the fish stalls. 'Grey Crow left this.' The note had *less* text than I expected — just four numbers. But those four numbers meant the city's hidden grid was already mapped.
less:2.cnHint: 阿栗在夜市鱼摊边递给我一张纸条，上面的内容比想象中____得多。
less:2.hook: Four numbers, and suddenly every exit felt watched.
less:2.line: '*Less* text means someone already knows you will understand.'

information:2.en: A cracked screen glowed under a noodle cart. Someone had taped a data chip to its base. I pried it free. Grey Crow had warned me: in Harbor City, raw *information* was worth more than any weapon. I slipped it into my coat and kept walking, eyes forward.
information:2.cnHint: 我在摊车底部发现了一枚芯片，里面的____价值连城。
information:2.hook: Behind me, boots splashed through puddles — getting closer.
information:2.line: '*Information* like this gets people disappeared,' Grey Crow had said.

paragraph:2.en: The wall beside the tea stall was covered in coded graffiti. Most was noise. But one short *paragraph* near the drain pipe was different — clean lines, deliberate spacing. Ali grabbed my sleeve. 'That wasn't there this morning.' Someone had written a warning in plain sight, hidden inside a city of symbols.
paragraph:2.cnHint: 茶摊旁的墙上出现了一个可疑的____，今早还不存在。
paragraph:2.line: 'Read that *paragraph* again — the last line changed.'

look:2.en: Grey Crow handed me a broken compass at the edge of the lantern market. Its *look* was ordinary — dull metal, scratched glass — but the needle spun in patterns, not north. Ali said nothing. She only watched the crowd. Something about that compass was coded, and I had ten minutes to read it.
look:2.cnHint: 灰鸦给我一个外____普通的罗盘，但指针的转动藏着密码。
look:2.hook: The needle stopped — pointing straight at Zero.
look:2.line: 'Don't let its *look* fool you; it never points to north.'

benefit:2.en: Zero stepped from the shadow of a silk stall and offered me a dry smile. 'Work with me tonight. There is real *benefit* in it for you — safe passage out of the east docks.' I said nothing. Grey Crow had told me Zero never offered a deal unless he needed something first.
benefit:2.cnHint: 零点提出合作，声称我会从中得到____，但他另有所图。
benefit:2.hook: Safe passage — or a neat trap with a ribbon on it.
benefit:2.line: 'The *benefit* to you is simple: you walk away clean.'

contain:2.en: Ali cracked the metal case open under the awning of a spice stall. Inside, a glass vial — small, sealed, cold. 'What does it *contain*?' I asked. She tilted it toward the neon light. A single strip of film curled inside, dense with micro-print. Grey Crow's voice came through my earpiece: 'Do not break the seal.'
contain:2.cnHint: 阿栗打开金属盒，里面的小瓶____着一卷密密麻麻的微缩胶卷。
contain:2.hook: Grey Crow's voice cut off before he could say why.
contain:2.line: 'Whatever you do, don't let it *contain* any heat.'

direction:2.en: The signal came through my earpiece as static, then three short tones. Grey Crow's voice followed, low and clipped: 'Switch *direction*.' I was heading toward the clock bridge. I stopped, turned, and took the alley behind the salt vendors instead. Thirty seconds later, two figures crossed the bridge where I had just been standing.
direction:2.cnHint: 灰鸦通过耳机指令我改变____，让我避开了尾随者。
direction:2.hook: Those two figures paused and scanned the crowd — hunting.

attach:2.en: The package sat on the wet counter of a closed dumpling stall, wrapped in brown paper. Ali pointed to a small strip of magnetic tape someone had used to *attach* a second layer beneath the wrapping. 'That's a tracker,' she said flatly. I set it down without a word. Zero had found us first.
attach:2.cnHint: 包裹底部____着一条追踪磁条，是零点提前布下的。
attach:2.hook: Somewhere in the crowd, Zero was already watching the signal move.
attach:2.line: 'They *attach* trackers to everything they want you to carry.'

actually:2.en: The night market hummed with coded lights. Ali pressed a cracked data chip into my hand. 'Grey Crow said this was a map,' she whispered. I scanned it. The chip was *actually* a distress signal — looping, silent, aimed at no one I knew.
actually:2.cnHint: 阿里交给我一枚芯片，我发现它____是一段求救信号。
actually:2.hook: The signal was still live, and someone else was already listening.
actually:2.line: 'This is *actually* a warning, not a map.'

themselves:2.en: I moved through the market stalls, watching the vendors. They spoke in clipped, careful syllables, never finishing a sentence aloud. The traders here had trained *themselves* to say everything in half-words — the other half lived in the encrypted static between signs.
themselves:2.cnHint: 这里的摊贩训练____用半句话交流，另一半藏在噪音里。
themselves:2.hook: One vendor's eyes locked on mine, and he stopped mid-syllable.
themselves:2.line: 'They taught *themselves* to hide words in silence.'

person:2.en: Grey Crow left a single burned match on the wet counter of stall seven. In this city, that meant exactly one thing: someone had been erased. Not their data, not their record — the *person* themselves, pulled out of every network, every camera, every trace.
person:2.cnHint: 七号摊上一根烧焦的火柴意味着某个____从所有网络中消失了。
person:2.line: 'A *person* who vanishes here never comes back.'

without:2.en: I found the note folded inside a hollow ceramic fish at the back of the market. Four words, printed in cold type: LEAVE NOW. Then, *without* a sender, without a seal — just blank space where a name should have been, loud as a shout in the rain.
without:2.cnHint: 我发现了一张____署名的纸条，上面只有四个字：立刻离开。
without:2.hook: Behind me, a stall light clicked off, then another.
without:2.line: 'You got a warning *without* a name — that means run.'

among:2.en: Ali crouched at the edge of the canal and pointed. Dozens of paper lanterns drifted on the black water. *Among* them, one burned blue instead of orange. Blue meant a dead-drop. Someone had placed a message here for me, hidden in plain sight, floating past indifferent eyes.
among:2.cnHint: 在漂流的灯笼____，一盏蓝色的灯是专门留给我的秘密信息。
among:2.hook: The blue lantern was already pulling toward the dark tunnel.
among:2.line: '*Among* all those lights, only the blue one matters.'

suppose:2.en: I stared at the coordinates scratched onto the underside of a noodle bowl. Zero had left them — had to be. 'I *suppose* he wants a meeting,' Grey Crow said behind me, voice dry as static. In Harbor City, an uninvited meeting was another word for a trap.
suppose:2.cnHint: 碗底刻着坐标，格雷·克劳____那是零点想要见面的暗示。
suppose:2.hook: The coordinates pointed to the one block every investigator avoided.
suppose:2.line: 'I *suppose* Zero chose this spot on purpose.'

health:2.en: The pharmacy stall glowed green in the rain. Rows of pills labeled CALM, FOCUS, SLEEP — nothing for what I had. The vendor slid a small card across the counter without a word. On it: a single frequency. 'For the *health* of your mind,' he said. 'Or what's left of it.'
health:2.cnHint: 药摊老板递给我一张卡片，说这个频率有益于我的____。
health:2.hook: The frequency matched the one Grey Crow told me never to tune into.
health:2.line: '*Health* of the mind matters more than the body here.'

mean:2.en: Grey Crow's last transmission was three short beeps and a long one. Simple. Old. I had to dig through a paper codebook Ali carried in her coat. When I found the pattern, my hands went cold. Three short, one long — it didn't *mean* help was coming. It meant goodbye.
mean:2.cnHint: 我查出那串信号____的内容后，手顿时凉了。
mean:2.hook: Grey Crow never said goodbye without a reason.
mean:2.line: 'Three short, one long — do you know what they *mean*?'

end:2.en: The night market stretched deep into Pier Nine, stalls packed so tight you could barely breathe. I followed the wire of coded lanterns all the way to the *end* of the row, where the last booth stood dark and shuttered. A folded paper sat on the counter, sealed with grey wax.
end:2.cnHint: 我追踪暗码灯笼，走到摊位的____，发现了一张封蜡纸条。
end:2.hook: The wax seal carried a crow's footprint — Grey Crow's mark.
end:2.line: 'The answer is always at the *end* of the line,' Grey Crow had warned me.

important:2.en: Ali pressed a small chip into my palm, her eyes scanning the crowded stalls behind me. 'This is *important*,' she said quietly, voice cut by the hiss of a nearby noodle cart. The chip held encrypted data — the kind Zero's crew paid fortunes to erase from existence.
important:2.cnHint: 阿里悄悄递给我一枚芯片，告诉我这件事非常____。
important:2.hook: Somewhere in the crowd, a shadow turned and walked the other way too fast.
important:2.line: 'Do not lose it — this is *important* enough to kill for.'

cause:2.en: A cracked speaker above the fish stall looped the same three notes on a six-second cycle. Grey Crow told me repeating signals in the market were never accidents. A looped tone at that frequency could *cause* the old grid sensors to log a false patrol route, clearing a path through the docks unseen.
cause:2.cnHint: 那段循环音频会____网格传感器记录错误路线，为我们开路。
cause:2.hook: The notes stopped — someone had found the speaker first.
cause:2.line: 'One wrong tone can *cause* the whole grid to turn blind.'

accord:2.en: Zero slid a folded card across the wet counter of the tea stall without a word. I read it twice. The terms were simple: stay out of the eastern docks, and he would stay out of my case. It was not trust — it was an *accord*, cold and thin as the rain on the tin roof above us.
accord:2.cnHint: 零点递来一张纸条，提出了一份冷冰冰的____，要我离开东码头。
accord:2.hook: I folded the card — and knew I would break the deal by dawn.
accord:2.line: 'Call it an *accord*. Break it, and I will not warn you again.'

result:2.en: I ran the chip Ali gave me through the pocket reader, standing shoulder-deep in the spice smoke of the market. The screen blinked once, then filled with a list of names and grid codes. The *result* was worse than anything I had expected: six surveillance nodes, all pointed at our safe house.
result:2.cnHint: 我扫描芯片，____显示六个监控节点正对准我们的藏身处。
result:2.hook: One of the names on the list was Ali's.
result:2.line: 'Look at the *result* — someone has been watching us for weeks.'

recent:2.en: The vendor at the map stall spread a laminated sheet of Pier Nine across the counter. I asked about *recent* changes to the dock layout. He tapped a freshly inked section near the north gate — a new corridor, unmarked on any public chart, cut through what used to be a dead-end alley.
recent:2.cnHint: 我询问____的码头变化，摊主指向一条不在公开地图上的新走廊。
recent:2.hook: The ink on that section was still tacky under my fingertip.
recent:2.line: 'I only mark *recent* changes. What you see there is very new.'

start:2.en: Grey Crow met me under the lantern pole at the market entrance and handed me a data card without ceremony. 'This is where it all began,' he said. The card held a single audio file — a broadcast fragment from three years ago, the *start* of every coded signal Zero had sent since.
start:2.cnHint: 灰鸦交给我一张卡片，里面存有一切暗号的____。
start:2.hook: The voice in the recording was one I already knew.
start:2.line: 'Find the *start* of the signal chain and you find the source.'

however:2.en: The stall owner swore he had seen nothing unusual near the north gate all week. His shop log showed quiet, steady sales — tea, dried fish, circuit tape. *However*, the mud on the side path told a different story: boot tracks, heavy and close together, pressed deep into the soft ground just last night.
however:2.cnHint: 店主声称一切正常，____泥地上的靴印证明昨夜有人经过。
however:2.hook: The tracks led straight under the locked service door.
however:2.line: '*However* calm it looks, the ground does not lie.'

human:2.en: The night market hummed with vendors and smoke. Ali pressed a cracked data-chip into my hand. 'This fell from Zero's coat,' she whispered. On it, one file: a list of names — every one tagged NOT *HUMAN*. My pulse spiked. What were they, if not us?
human:2.cnHint: 阿栗交给我一块数据芯片，里面的名单让我怀疑这些人究竟是不是____。
human:2.hook: The last name on the list was mine.
human:2.line: 'Every name here is marked NOT *HUMAN* — so what are we?'

large:2.en: Grey Crow met me beneath the neon fish stalls, rain hammering the iron roof. He unrolled a *large* paper map — rare, physical, impossible to hack. Red circles marked six points across Harbor City. 'Zero moves tonight,' he said, tapping the widest circle. 'We have one hour.'
large:2.cnHint: 灰鸦展开一张____的纸质地图，标出了零点今晚的行动范围。
large:2.hook: The widest red circle was drawn around my building.
large:2.line: 'A *large* map — old-school, unhackable, and it says you're the target.'

view:2.en: I climbed the old signal tower at the edge of Harbor City's night market. From up here, the *view* of a thousand glowing stalls stretched below like a living circuit board. Grey Crow had told me: the message was hidden somewhere in that light. I just had to find it.
view:2.cnHint: 我爬上信号塔，试图从高处的____中找到隐藏的信息。
view:2.hook: One light blinked in a pattern no one else had noticed.
view:2.line: 'The *view* from above never lies — look for the odd light out.'

social:2.en: Ali handed me a cracked data-chip. 'Every *social* broadcast in the market runs through this node,' she said quietly. I pressed it into my scanner. Hundreds of voices, coded and layered, filled my ears at once. Zero's signal was buried somewhere inside — I was sure of it.
social:2.cnHint: 阿里给我一块芯片，它连接着夜市所有的____广播网络。
social:2.hook: One voice repeated a single word, over and over, in perfect silence.
social:2.line: 'The *social* network here hides more secrets than the police ever guessed.'

skill:2.en: The lock on the back gate of stall forty-seven was old, but clever. Grey Crow watched as I worked. 'Pure *skill*,' he said, with something close to approval. The mechanism clicked open. Inside, a folded paper waited on an empty shelf — the kind of message people used before signals existed.
skill:2.cnHint: 我凭借____打开了一把复杂的旧锁，发现了里面藏着的纸条。
skill:2.hook: The paper held only four words, and my name was the last.
skill:2.line: 'That *skill* of yours just opened a door Zero thought was sealed.'

job:2.en: Ali spread the map across the noodle stall's wet counter. 'Our *job* tonight is simple,' she said, tracing a red line with one finger. 'Find the drop point before Zero does.' Simple, she called it. The drop point was somewhere inside a market of ten thousand strangers.
job:2.cnHint: 阿里解释了我们今晚的____：在零点之前找到那个交接地点。
job:2.hook: The red line on the map ended at a stall that sold nothing.
job:2.line: 'Our *job* is to reach that point first — every second counts now.'

business:2.en: The tea seller at stall twelve had been in this market for thirty years. I asked about the locked room behind his counter. 'Not your *business*,' he said, eyes steady. But his hand moved to cover something small and flat on the shelf — and that small move told me everything I needed.
business:2.cnHint: 茶摊老板告诉我那间上锁的房间不是我的____，但他的举动出卖了他。
business:2.hook: Whatever lay on that shelf, someone wanted it badly enough to kill.
business:2.line: 'That room is my *business* alone — walk away while you still can.'

eat:2.en: Grey Crow sat across from me at a street stall, pushing food around his plate. 'You have to *eat*,' he said, without looking up. 'Long night ahead.' Under his bowl, half hidden by a paper napkin, lay a key — old brass, no label. He said nothing more. He never did.
eat:2.cnHint: 格雷·克劳催我____，却悄悄在碗底藏了一把神秘的钥匙。
eat:2.hook: The key fit no lock I had ever seen — yet.
eat:2.line: '*Eat* something now; once we move, there will be no stopping.'

healthy:2.en: The medical stall near the east gate looked ordinary — bright lights, clean shelves. But every price was wrong by exactly one digit. Ali leaned close. 'A *healthy* shop with bad numbers is a shop with two sets of books,' she whispered. Behind the counter, a second screen glowed with data that had nothing to do with medicine.
healthy:2.cnHint: 一家看似____的医疗摊位账目有误，暗藏着另一套秘密数据。
healthy:2.hook: The second screen showed names — and mine was near the top.
healthy:2.line: 'A *healthy* front is the oldest trick; check what they hide behind it.'

place:2.en: Grey Crow's message was three words: find the *place*. No address, no map marker — just those three words on a scrap of foil tucked inside my scanner case. I had walked this market a hundred times. Only one spot had no stall, no seller, no light. A gap in the grid. That had to be it.
place:2.cnHint: 格雷·克劳的纸条只写了三个字：找到那个____。
place:2.hook: The gap in the grid was exactly one person wide, and someone was already standing in it.
place:2.line: 'This *place* was left empty on purpose — someone planned for us to come.'

likely:2.en: The night market stall sold data chips wrapped in fish paper. Grey Crow slid one across the wet counter. 'This is *likely* the last copy,' he said, eyes scanning the crowd. Ali caught it without looking. Someone nearby was already watching us.
likely:2.cnHint: 灰鸦在夜市摊位给了我一枚芯片，说这____ 是最后一份。
likely:2.hook: The watcher melted into the crowd before I could turn.
likely:2.line: 'This is *likely* the only copy left in Harbor City.'

experience:2.en: A fog of frying oil and burnt wire filled the night market. Ali knelt by a cracked wall panel, fingers reading the circuits. 'My *experience* says this was forced open six hours ago,' she said. The panel hid a small hollow — and inside it, a folded paper map.
experience:2.cnHint: 阿里凭借____，判断出墙板暗格被人撬开才六小时。
experience:2.hook: The map showed a building that no longer existed.
experience:2.line: 'My *experience* tells me someone was here very recently.'

lot:2.en: Zero left a *lot* of things behind — a cracked lens, three dead signal tags, a half-eaten rice cake still warm. Each item was placed too neatly to be accidental. Ali photographed them in silence. I counted seven pieces in total and felt the cold weight of a message.
lot:2.cnHint: 零点留下了____东西，每一件摆放得如此整齐，根本不像偶然。
lot:2.hook: The seventh item was addressed to me by name.
lot:2.line: 'A *lot* of clues, all pointing at the same door.'

public:2.en: The message was painted on a *public* water tank at the market entrance, three metres high, in glow ink visible only under rain. Anyone could have seen it. That was the point. Ali read it first and went quiet. Grey Crow said the words were a code used by people who had disappeared.
public:2.cnHint: 信息被写在____水塔上，所有人都能看见，但只有少数人能读懂。
public:2.hook: Grey Crow's hand trembled as he read the final line.
public:2.line: 'They chose a *public* wall so we could not ignore it.'

example:2.en: Grey Crow pointed to a vendor's sign painted with strange punctuation. 'Take this as an *example*,' he said. 'Every third symbol is a letter.' Ali copied them fast. When the hidden letters were read together they spelled a dock number. The vendor had not looked up once.
example:2.cnHint: 灰鸦以摊贩招牌为____，教我识别隐藏在标点里的字母密码。
example:2.hook: The dock number belonged to a ship listed as sunk.
example:2.line: 'Use this sign as an *example* — the code is in the gaps.'

whether:2.en: The sealed box sat under a noodle cart, tagged with a blinking blue light. I did not know *whether* to open it or leave it for the next contact. Ali said nothing. Grey Crow had already walked away. The blue light blinked once more, then stopped. A decision could not wait.
whether:2.cnHint: 我不知道____该打开那个盒子，时间不等人。
whether:2.hook: Inside was a voice chip that held my own voice.
whether:2.line: 'Tell me *whether* you opened the box or walked away.'

focus:2.en: Noise was everywhere — vendors shouting, rain hammering tin roofs, drones humming. I forced my *focus* onto one sound: a low repeating tone under the market's surface, like a buried radio. Ali heard it too. We followed it past three stalls and stopped at a locked iron grate in the ground.
focus:2.cnHint: 在嘈杂的夜市中，我将____集中在一个隐约的地下声响上。
focus:2.hook: The grate was warm, and the lock had been cut from the inside.
focus:2.line: 'Keep your *focus* on the low sound — ignore everything else.'

avoid:2.en: Grey Crow mapped a route through the market on my palm with one finger. 'You must *avoid* the lamp posts on the east row,' he said. 'Each one carries a face scanner.' I memorised the path in seconds. Ali was already moving. The lamps turned slowly, hunting.
avoid:2.cnHint: 灰鸦告诉我要____东排路灯，因为每盏灯都装有人脸扫描器。
avoid:2.hook: One lamp stopped turning and locked its lens on me.
avoid:2.line: '*Avoid* the east row lamps — they are already active.'
